subject: Commit criteria & validation for compute island (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Sana Qureshi <sana@biogenix.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@biogenix.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up and artifacts from today's infra discovery

Mina / Ben - thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of attachments (SLA_Requirements.xlsx + a rough architecture sketch) attached. High-level pain points we covered:

- Production latency spikes during batch inference and slow warm-up from cold KV cache; 95th p99 for some endpoints is high and unpredictable.
- Multi-tenant risk: we need strict tenant isolation for models handling PHI / clinical notes (HIPAA).
- Scaling: we expect variable daily traffic with 4x spikes weekly during model retrain rollouts. Need reserved capacity + burst policy.
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence, KMS integration, and audit logs are must-haves.

Goals we articulated internally:
- Target 95th percentile latency < 150ms for 512-token runs (baseline model).
- Sustained throughput ~120 tokens/sec per logical worker for our primary endpoint; burst up to 400 tokens/sec across the pool.
- SLA window for uptime: 99.9% monthly; credits negotiable for outages.

Immediate asks from BioGenix:
1) A short written summary of the commit criteria Redwood would need to reserve an isolated pool (GPU count, expected throughput, fallback behavior).
2) A pricing ballpark for a 12-month reserved pool + burst credits.
3) Confirmation on data-at-rest encryption, KMS support, and audit log retention options.

We have procurement on copy (procurement@biogenix.ai) and Tom (CTO) is looped for technical sign-off. Can you reply with a proposed next step cadence (technical deep-dive + security questionnaire + SOC2 artifacts)?

Thanks,
Sana Qureshi
VP Product, BioGenix Therapeutics

Attachments: SLA_Requirements.xlsx, bio_architecture_sketch.png

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sana Qureshi <sana@biogenix.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, procurement@biogenix.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up and artifacts from today's infra discovery

Sana - great to meet the team today. Appreciate the attachments; they're helpful. Below is our recap + proposed commit criteria and immediate next steps so you have a single doc to share with procurement and engineering.

Recap (short):
- Pain: inconsistent tail latency under variable load and cold-start KV misses.
- Constraint: strict PHI isolation requirement + SOC2/KMS/Auditability.
- Target: 95p < 150ms for 512-token runs; sustained pool throughput to support baseline traffic with 4x burst capability.

Redwood proposed commit criteria for an isolated reserved pool (we recommend a staged validation):
1) Capacity & sizing
   - Initial reservation: 8x A100-class GPUs (single tenant isolated pool) - expected baseline throughput ~960k tokens/min across the pool (estimate depends on model variant).
   - Burst overlay: allow up to additional 4x GPU-equivalent credits for spikes (auto-burst to shared capacity with fallback policy).
2) Isolation & security
   - Dedicated tenant pool (no co-tenancy on the vGPU layer), encrypted disks, full KMS integration; separate network ACLs (VPC peering option).
   - Audit log export to your SIEM; 365-day retention standard for Enterprise plan (custom retention can be arranged).
3) SLOs & SLA
   - Latency SLO: 95th < 150ms for standard payloads (we'll supply a validation harness).
   - Uptime SLA: 99.9% monthly; credit tiers defined in draft SLA.
4) Validation & rollout
   - Phase 1: Technical deep-dive + synthetic load tests (we'll run your prompt set and our calibration harness).
   - Phase 2: Canary run on reserved pool with production shadow traffic for 72 hours.
   - Phase 3: Full cutover and inclusion in reserved orchestration + burst policy.

Operational notes / assumptions:
- Model: we expect to serve a tuned open model; final throughput numbers depend on sequence length and quantization.
- KV caching: recommended warm-up strategies and prefix caching for retrain rollouts to reduce cold-start cost.
- Pricing: I'll have pricing ballpark in the next message - depends on commitment length and burst mechanics.

Next steps (proposed timeline):
- Week 1: Technical deep-dive (60-90m) - include Tom + your infra lead; we'll bring our runtime lead.
- Within 48h after the call: Security questionnaire + SOC2 evidence packet (we'll share a download link).
- Week 2: Synthetic validation window + canary schedule planning.

I'll pull together a short one-pager with the sizing assumptions and a draft SLA (attaching redwood_sla_draft.pdf). Ben - can you add any ops constraints we should call out? Jordan - can you confirm availability for the technical deep-dive next Tue/Wed?

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_sla_draft.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Sana Qureshi <sana@biogenix.ai>, procurement@biogenix.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 17:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up and artifacts from today's infra discovery

Quick ops notes to add to the record - low-friction items and a couple of gating items:

- Low friction:
  - KMS: we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer-hosted HSM integrations. We'll need the KMS key ARN and an integration window during provisioning.
  - Audit logs: structured logs (JSON) exported to S3/GCS or pushed to your Splunk/Datadog via our export connector.

- Gating / validation items:
  - Workload profile: we need a representative 24-48h sample of requests (anonymized) to validate sequence-length distribution.
  - Warm-up plan: recommend a pre-warm (synthetic prefix cache load) before canary. If you can't provide traces, we'll use our worst-case synthetic profile and surface differences.
  - Canaries: 72h is baseline; if production traffic has high variance we may extend to 7 days for full regression confidence.

Operational checklist I'll own for the deep-dive:
- Pull SOC2 artifact bundle and pre-populate your security questionnaire.
- Coordinate with infra to provision isolated pool + KMS access window.
- Run an initial benchmark and share token/sec and p95/p99 latency matrix.

I'll mark tentative time slots Tue 9-11am PT and Wed 1-3pm PT for the technical deep-dive. Sana - let us know which works.

--Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sana Qureshi <sana@biogenix.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Thanks, Mina and Ben - this is exactly what we needed. Procurement is okay to proceed to the next step once we have:
1) The written sizing assumptions and pricing ballpark for 12-month commitment (we can sign an NDA if helpful).
2) A link to the SOC2 bundle and the security questionnaire pre-filled where possible.
3) A confirmation of the deep-dive timeslot - Tue 9-11am PT works for Tom and our infra lead.

Procurement point of contact: Elena Park <procurement@biogenix.ai> (she's on copy).

One more ask: please create a short mutual action plan (MAP) doc with milestones, owners, and estimated dates we can attach to our procurement packet. If you can include the DocuSign NDA link in the MAP, procurement can fast-track the paperwork.

I'll upload the anonymized 48h trace sample by Monday EOD to the secure share link (I'll send separately).

Sana
Sana Qureshi
VP Product, BioGenix Therapeutics
